answers.text: Have the assistant give three lines every time, same order — drop-off time, pallet count, then damage — one fact per line.
List the calls with customer, topic and outcome for whoever needs the follow-up list.
The timing at the end doesn't quite add up given when the crew starts and how long the job takes.
The finance numbers looked about right to me, nothing jumped out.
I'd pick the second one, it shows the actual ticket numbers behind the percentage.
I'd send the second email since it has real volume figures in it. The first one doesn't say by how much, so it's hard to check.
1. No. 2. Yes. 3. No. 4. Not sure. 5. No.
I'd leave out the rates and be careful with the confidentiality clause since it names the client.
Before it's sent out each month I'd check the total against the system record.
The last step worries me most, since once the payment note goes through automatically that's hard to undo. The first step matters too, if the invoice gets read wrong everything after is off.
